question: Does a resident have the right to speak at a city council meeting, and can the council limit that?

must_include: address a meeting|address the public body|speak|public comment

notes: Right to address the public body — a frequent and contentious counter question. [REVISED: my first expectation used citizen wording. MCL 15.263(5) actually says a person 'shall be permitted to address a meeting of a public body under rules established and recorded by the public body' — so the answer is yes, subject to the body's recorded rules. ALSO EXPOSED A REAL DEFECT: with citizen phrasing ('speak at a city council meeting') the first OMA chunk retrieves at rank 10 and 18 of 40 hits are Election Law; with statutory phrasing it retrieves at rank 1. Citizen vocabulary is exactly the vocabulary this tool must handle at the counter.]
